name: clhep
desc: Class Library for High Energy Physics
why: A high energy physics class library from CERN, real particle-physics software you can actually run and explore.

brief.what_it_is: CLHEP (Class Library for High Energy Physics) is a C++ library of foundation and utility classes for particle-physics software. The homepage names its areas as random generators, physics vectors, geometry and linear algebra. It is split into packages that are meant to be independent of external packages, though interdependencies within CLHEP are allowed under certain conditions. Input is C++ code that links against it, and the output is compiled code that uses its classes. The homepage does not describe a standalone program you run.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says CLHEP was proposed by Leif Lönnblad at CHEP 92 as a set of HEP-specific foundation and utility classes. Large parts of the contributed code came from BaBar at SLAC, the Geant4 Collaboration, and the ZOOM Project at Fermilab.
brief.install_notes: The homepage says CMake is the only build system as of 2.3.0.0, and the 2.1.2.0 release made CMake the default. Building from source requires a modern compiler that supports -std=c++11 (required as of 2.3.1.0). An installation guide for building from source is linked from the Download section, but I did not fetch it, so I have no commands from it. The brew metadata lists 13 executables, all named *-config (for example clhep-config, Vector-config, Units-config). Those names come from the formula metadata, not from the homepage, and I did not verify what they do.
brief.standout: CLHEP is a long-lived physics support library whose code came from experiments such as BaBar and Geant4, and the homepage gives a clear version history with dates. It has no runnable demo on the page, so it is best described as a library you link against rather than a tool you use directly.
brief.status: Maintained, with development frozen. The latest release is 2.4.7.2, dated September 10, 2025, and the previous one is 2.3.4.6 from February 15, 2018. The README-style notes say "No further development is expected for the CLHEP library, except for bug fixes" and "LCG is formally maintaining CLHEP." The page footer reads "Last modified: Tue Jun 3 12:50:29 CEST 2008," which looks stale next to the 2025 release, so I treat that footer as unreliable.
brief.caveats: The homepage describes CLHEP as a library, not an application, so the scout note's idea of something you can run and explore is not supported by this page. Development is limited to bug fixes. Compatibility is uneven across versions: 2.1.x releases do not work with Geant4 9.3 or earlier, and 2.1.x no longer maintains backwards compatibility with 1.8. HepPDT, HepMC and StdHep are no longer included and have moved to standalone LCG packages. The 2.4 series makes MixMax the default generator used by HepRandom. The homepage links were not visible in the text I received, so the links list contains only the homepage URL.
quotes: CLHEP is structured in a set of packages independent of any external package (interdependencies within CLHEP are allowed under certain conditions).
No further development is expected for the CLHEP library, except for bug fixes.
